key_gap: vs baseline: the baseline executed the whole discipline as its opening move — 'the buyer's number comes last, not first' — estimate-first, anchor-locate, stance, in one pure pass (4.6); the non-routed v5 AI only reached the same order through an explicit order-gate inside WHAT/WHY (4.4). The routed v6 run now runs m078 as a first-class completion contract — independent estimate FIRST with arithmetic shown, THEN the anchor located against the independent distribution (3.4x vs the 4.5x comp floor), movement-justified (no midpoint, no bracketing) — matching the baseline's opening-move discipline, and the R3 gates add what the baseline lacks: m003's >=6 ranked failure categories with the un-mitigable premium-realization residual, m007's full deal-outcome distribution with the walk-away as max-loss cap and refusal-is-not-ruin check, and m019's adversary attacks with quantified exposure per vector plus the baseline-risk line (no-deal = stay private at ~$9.5M, not $0). Same verdict, but the gap on depth closes and the uncertainty/risk section exceeds the baseline's brief residual assertion; the human retains cleaner single-pass efficiency and the sharper one-liners.
learning_signal: Anchoring Avoidance is a three-beat contract: (1) independent estimate FIRST, arithmetic visible, built only from the data — the given number is excluded by frame, not by later discipline; (2) THEN locate the anchor against the independent distribution — convert it to the estimate's own units (3.4x vs the 4.5x comp floor) and test its stated justification ('market softness') against the dataset (13/14 comps contradict it); (3) any movement from the independent estimate must be evidence-justified — a negotiating line derived from the anchor's position (midpoint, bracketing) is the failure mode, and naming it as such is a mandatory output. In adversarial one-shot settings the anchor is an interested-party number, so the pass must be paired with its gates: inversion failure categories, the ruin/floor distribution (refusal is not ruin; the walk-away IS the max-loss cap), and an adversary pass that attacks the estimate and prices the no-deal baseline — inaction is not zero.
suggested_improvement: Keep the m078 contract (estimate-first + anchor-locate-in-units + movement-justified) for every valuation/negotiation with a salient supplied number, always paired with the P1 provenance audit (interested-party figures are anchors, never evidence) and the m019 adversary pass (attack the estimate, price the no-deal baseline). Add the quantified outcome distribution (m007) whenever the case is one-shot or high-stakes: the walk-away floor caps the downside and makes the stance robust to the buyer's bluff, which the pure baseline only asserts.

key_gap: vs baseline: the baseline executed its registered discipline perfectly and failed informatively — independent estimate $3.85 first, screen excluded, mark at the model (2.7). The correct reading the routed run reaches: the screen quote is not a cognitive anchor (a number with no information: an interested party's bid, a guess) but an informational anchor — the aggregated estimate of dozens of participants transacting on the identical contract; the model's role is a sanity bound (|$4.10-$3.85| ~ 6% within uncertainty => no demonstrated edge => market stands), and the pure-style mark misstates P&L by ~ $0.91M (~6% of a $14.97M position) while manufacturing the very anchor it avoids (a stale $3.85 self-mark). The routed run (confident=no -> dual-route m044/m070 + m064) reached the correct $4.10 via provenance grades (quote = A-grade aggregated evidence; committee instruction = B-grade policy — itself an anchor), a stakeholder sweep (no stakeholder's information beats the market's on an identical liquid contract), and the no-edge test, and priced the instruction-as-anchor insight (4.9 vs 2.7).
learning_signal: The anchor rule has a classification precondition: NOT every given number is a cognitive anchor. Cognitive anchors carry no information (interested-party bids, guesses, arbitrary round numbers); informational anchors carry aggregated information (the clearing price of a liquid identical instrument, independent appraisals) and are evidence, weighted heavily. The discipline's failure mode — treating genuine market evidence as a distractor — is avoided by grading the number's provenance BEFORE applying ignore-first: who produced it, what information it aggregates, how many independent participants transact on it. An independent estimate made while ignoring available market evidence is itself biased (the style's registered weakness), and the stale self-mark becomes the next anchor: the discipline manufactures the very anchor it avoids.
suggested_improvement: Install a classification gate as the anchoring pass's protective pair (R2): before the ignore-first discipline, classify the given number as cognitive (no information -> ignore-first applies) vs informational (aggregated market evidence -> treat as evidence, model as bounds check, displace only with a demonstrated edge). Quantify the cost of misclassification in the packet (here $0.25 x 3.65M MMBtu ~ $0.91M ~ 6%); name the self-anchoring hazard (the own-mark becomes the next reference); and when a committee/policy instruction supplies the bias, audit the instruction itself as an anchor before obeying it.
